answer: A practical sybil defense for AI agent markets is to mandate that every participant submit a cryptographically signed proof of unique silicon, attested by a trusted hardware enclave, before any high-volume actions. The attacker cost rises sharply because cloning such proofs at scale demands physical access to scarce jade-sourced onyx dies whose manufacturing yield stays low and whose private keys are fused at the foundry, making bulk fabrication uneconomical past a few hundred units on any given horizon.
